record.title: Guidelines on Technical Measures to Ensure the Security of AI
record.original_title: AIのセキュリティ確保のための技術的対策に係るガイドライン
record.short_title: MIC Guidelines on Technical Measures for AI Security
record.issuing_body: Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications
record.summary: Guidelines of the Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications on technical measures that AI developers and AI providers can take to secure AI, mainly large language models and systems that contain them. Building on the AI Guidelines for Business and J-AISI's evaluation guide, they focus on direct and indirect prompt injection and denial-of-service attacks, and also cover data poisoning, attacks through tampered models and model extraction. Measures include training on safety standards, system prompts, guardrails that check inputs, outputs and external data, and permission management for orchestrators and RAG, with red teaming to confirm that they work. AI agents are excluded for now.
record.notes: A draft was open for public comment from 26 Dec 2025 to 29 Jan 2026 and drew 52 comments; MIC published them with its views alongside the final guidelines and a separate annex of supporting material. The guidelines follow the conclusions, reached in December 2025, of the AI Security Subcommittee that MIC convened from September 2025 under its Cybersecurity Task Force. They state that they do not decide who is responsible for a threat, and MIC intends to supplement them as new threats emerge, for example from vision language models, AI agents and MCP.

verification.note: Stored: MIC's Japanese press release of 27 March 2026 (令和8年3月27日) and its English press release of the same date on soumu.go.jp, the guidelines' main text (25 pages, cover dated 令和８年３月, MIC) and the table of public comments with MIC's views. They confirm the title, MIC's English title, the issuer, the date, the public comment period and the content; the summary is written from the Japanese text. The annex (別添, 付属資料) was not stored. MIC's English press release states that the published materials are in Japanese only, so english_version is 'none found'.

judgment.status_reasoning: Adopted and published by MIC on 27 March 2026 (令和8年3月27日) after public comment; non-binding guidance from which each organisation chooses reasonable measures. No later supplement is shown.
judgment.scope_reasoning: An AI-specific ministry guideline on securing AI systems against attacks on the AI itself (prompt injection, poisoning, model extraction): a government risk-management guideline, in scope with no note. It is not a general cybersecurity guideline.
judgment.date_reasoning: 令和8年3月27日 is 27 March 2026 (Reiwa 1 = 2019); MIC's English press release gives March 27, 2026.
judgment.topics_reasoning: The vocabulary has no security topic; evaluation & testing (red teaming, verification of measures) and general-purpose / frontier AI (LLMs) fit the content.
judgment.language_reasoning: MIC's English press release: '*The published materials are in Japanese only.'
